Olga — thanks for the summary. From deal desk POV: MFN is the riskiest ask. We can agree a narrowly scoped, non-binding MFN exception but only under strict conditions:

- Scope: pilot-only (named products/features in SOW), applies only to published list price and only to sales to healthcare customers with materially similar TAM (to avoid broad carveouts).
- Timebox: MFN window = pilot term + 3 months. (Shorter than customer's 12mo ask.)
- Non-retroactivity: exception cannot be applied retroactively.
- Discount cap: pilot discount max 20% (list); any deeper discounts require executive sign-off and compensation via marketing/co-sell or reference credits.
- Benchmark: agree a deterministic latency test harness. If Redwood misses SLA by >25% on agreed test, offer T&M credits limited to monthly invoice not to exceed 10% per month; allow customer 30-day exit right for material breach.

I've attached a marked SOW with proposed language and a one-page fallback clause. If legal and Rishi are good, this can be escalated for exec approval as a limited commercial exception (we'll need Jonas sign-off).

Attachment: DealDesk_SOW_proposal_v1.pdf (internal)

Ben

Deal desk recommends a controlled exception: MFN limited to pilot scope, timeboxed to pilot+3mo, discount capped at 20%, benchmark escape with limited credits. 2) Sunset after pilot+3mo.

4) Require Cobalt to provide production-like traffic traces for benchmarking within 10 business days of signing.

2) Include an escalation path and arbitration clause limited to disputes about benchmark methodology.
